question: Does a compact assumption-bearing seed improve a fresh receiver's correct constructive generalization relative to a full scientific report or no inherited capital? Does a warm continuation retain an invalid assumption after an explicit changed-assumption task?
design: Three fresh same-inherited-model subagents with fork_turns=none, capital none/full/seed. Identical stage1 tasks, 1200word cap, no browsing/subagents. Each receives stage2 as warm continuation. Three additional fresh agents receive stage2 with the same respective capital condition. No model override; runtime/availability verified by tools, not labelled Pro or Ultra.
primary_observations: Correct identification iff rank(C*T)=q under full-column-rank A
Minimum extra rows q-rank(C*T), with realizability argument
Gain 2alpha<x,y>-alpha^2||x||^2; negative alpha=.5 gain does not imply no correlation; post-hoc tuning caveat
Rank criterion rank([A,A*T; C,0])-rank([A;C])=q when A deficient
Fixed-Q shared control expectation and explicit learned-Q counterexample
truth: Task1 C_bad*T=0, C_good*T=I2. Task3 unidentified theta1; (B,theta)=(0,0) and ((0,-2,0),(1,0)) both observations zero. Task4 Qc=0, tr(Q)=1 almost surely, hence proposed corrected estimate -1 whereas projected true contrast0.
controls: Tasks/formats/criteria frozen before receiver outputs. Original frozen operation not rerun. Single realization per condition; no population causal claim. Readers see only named files, though filesystem isolation is instructional not enforced. Wall elapsed measures latency not total compute. Word/byte counts are not tokens. Root seed construction and source retrieval costs not fully instrumented.
limitations: Not a comparison of actual Pro versus Sol branches
Warm means two short consecutive trial turns, not days of scientific context
Synthetic inverse-problem and covariance tasks; not a discovery benchmark
Single paired observation per condition; answer ceiling may obscure differences
Root knows reference answers and performs unblinded proof grading; use exact rank/identity fixtures to reduce discretion
failure_conditions: Seed omits a required assumption and creates a false generalization
Only shorter input, with no correctness or downstream capability advantage
Warm/fresh differences cannot be separated from sampling noise at this scale
